note: Rejudged against the whole RFC 2661 Section 5.8 sentence: "If no peer response is detected after several retransmissions, (a recommended default is 5, but SHOULD be configurable), the tunnel and all sessions within MUST be cleared." This RID is the configurable-budget SHOULD; the MUST-clear clause remains a separate obligation. Q1: TestRFC2661ConfiguredMaxRetransmitClearsTunnel explicitly sets the new-tunnel retransmit budget2, establishes a tunnel and leaves its HELLO unanswered. It asserts Established after both allowed retransmissions, then Closed and the StopCCN log at the next deadline. Q2: default5 instead of configured2 misses the final Closed assertion; early exhaustion misses one of the Established assertions. Existing panic records prove only reachability and this judgment does not claim a newly observed semantic red. Q3: hello-retries0 disables dead-peer detection, the controlled clock crosses each exponential-backoff deadline, and the reactor has no timer goroutine driving competing teardown. Q4: the test covers configurable count and its early/late boundary. ExtractParameters still defaults MaxRetransmit5 and parses the operator value; its18ea5e830a MRU-policy validation addition neither overwrites nor bypasses max-retransmit. The current valid configuration reaches its unchanged return. tunnelDefaults passes the setting; setMaxRetransmit changes the defaults for future tunnels; reliableConfig is consumed by incoming locateTunnelLocked and outgoing handleDial; ReliableEngine.Tick signals teardown only after the configured count is exceeded. The current two tag assertions retain their original scope. This static rejudgment ran no tests, recorder or stamp.
